title: Classical Complex Algebraic Actions and Affine Embeddings

items.title: Products of affine algebraic sets have tensor-product coordinate rings
items.statement: For affine algebraic sets X⊆C^m and Y⊆C^n, allowing empty or reducible sets, the map C[X]⊗C[Y]→C[X×Y], f⊗h ↦ ((x,y)↦f(x)h(y)), is an isomorphism; iterating gives the analogous three-factor identification. The argument is choice-free.
items.strategy: Surjectivity splits ambient polynomials into sums of products of separate-variable polynomials; injectivity writes a kernel element with independent second coefficients and evaluates on X, using the polynomial-function identification. Empty factors and the three-factor iteration are checked directly.

items.title: Classical complex affine algebraic actions and rational modules
items.statement: Fixes complex affine algebraic groups with the coordinate Hopf maps Δ, ε, S; algebraic left actions and equivariant morphisms; rational G-modules as linear actions in which every vector lies in a finite-dimensional stable subspace with algebraic action; the inverse-pullback function action (r(g)f)(x)=f(g⁻¹x); its right-comodule convention c:V→V⊗H; and the opposite direct-action pullback convention.
items.strategy: The tensor identification of product coordinate rings defines Δ, ε and S; the inverse-pullback action and its right-comodule form are distinguished from the direct-action pullback, and rationality is defined by finite-dimensional algebraic stability.

items.title: Affine actions correspond to coordinate-ring coactions
items.statement: Assume AC. Algebraic left actions of a complex affine algebraic group G on an affine algebraic set X correspond bijectively to unital algebra maps δ:A→H⊗A with (Δ⊗id)δ=(id⊗δ)δ and (ε⊗id)δ=id, via δ(f)(g,x)=f(gx); c=τ(S⊗id)δ is the equivalent right-comodule algebra structure with c(f)(x,g)=f(g⁻¹x), and equivariant morphisms correspond to coaction-intertwining algebra maps.
items.strategy: Pull back the action along the product-ring identification to obtain δ, use the affine algebra-morphism antiequivalence to reconstruct actions from δ, and convert to the inverse-action right comodule over the inversion morphism. AC is inherited only from the antiequivalence.

items.title: Every affine-group comodule is a union of finite-dimensional rational submodules
items.statement: Let G be a complex affine algebraic group and c:V→V⊗C[G] a right comodule. Every finite subset of V lies in a finite-dimensional subcomodule W; evaluation of c gives a linear G-action whose restriction to each such W is algebraic, so V is a directed union of finite-dimensional rational submodules. Choice-free.
items.strategy: Coassociativity plus a quotient map force the finite coefficient space of c(v) to be a subcomodule containing v; finite sums give directedness; matrix entries and inverse entries obtained by inversion exhibit an actual morphism to GL(W) without selecting an infinite basis.

items.title: The coordinate ring of an affine algebraic action is a locally finite rational module
items.statement: Assume AC. If a complex affine algebraic group G acts algebraically on an affine algebraic set X, then C[X] with (gf)(x)=f(g⁻¹x) is a rational G-module: every finite set of functions lies in a finite-dimensional stable subspace on which G acts algebraically, and the action preserves multiplication and the unit. No irreducibility or reductivity is assumed.
items.strategy: Apply the comodule finite-subspace lemma to the right-comodule algebra structure supplied by the action/coaction proposition; multiplicativity and unit preservation follow because the coaction is an algebra map. AC is inherited from the coaction dictionary.

items.title: Torus rational modules and affine actions are lattice gradings
items.statement: For T=(C*)^r with H=C[t_1^{±1},…,t_r^{±1}], right H-comodules (equivalently rational T-modules) correspond to direct-sum gradings V=⊕_m V_m, with c(v)=v⊗t^m on V_m and t·v=t^m v, and intertwining maps are exactly degree-preserving; a coordinate-ring action corresponds to a grading A=⊕_m A_m with 1∈A_0 and A_mA_n⊆A_{m+n}, and conversely every such grading of a finitely generated reduced complex algebra arises from an affine algebraic T-action. In the reconstruction assume AC; function weights are opposite to point weights, f(tx)=t^{−m}f(x) for f of degree m.
items.strategy: Unique Laurent coefficients give orthogonal idempotent projectors and a direct-sum decomposition with finite support, and conversely a grading defines a coaction; a rational module's coactions on finite-dimensional submodules glue by Laurent-polynomial determination. The algebra law is exactly A_mA_n⊆A_{m+n}; a reduced finite-type graded algebra is realized through the published Nullstellensatz and the dictionary reconstructs its action.

items.title: Every complex affine algebraic action has a finite-dimensional equivariant closed embedding
items.statement: Assume AC. For a complex affine algebraic group G acting algebraically on an affine algebraic set X, there is a finite-dimensional rational G-module W⊆C[X] generating C[X] as an algebra such that evaluation ι:X→W*, ι(x)(w)=w(x), is an equivariant isomorphism onto a closed invariant algebraic subset, the target carrying the dual action (gλ)(w)=λ(g⁻¹w). Neither connectedness, irreducibility, nor reductivity is required.
items.strategy: Put finitely many algebra generators in one finite-dimensional rational submodule W. The dual action is algebraic by transpose-inverse. The surjection C[z]→C[X] has radical kernel; the Nullstellensatz identifies its quotient with the closed set V(I) and the affine antiequivalence gives the inverse isomorphism. Evaluation is explicitly equivariant.

title: Classical Complex Algebraic Actions and Affine Embeddings — Examples

items.title: Opposite weights on the affine plane and its coordinate ring
items.statement: For T=C* acting on A^2 by t(x,y)=(tx,t⁻¹y), the coordinate action has degrees deg x=−1 and deg y=1, so x^a y^b has degree b−a and A_0=C[xy]; the generating submodule W=Cx+Cy gives the identity embedding into its dual plane, whose weights are (1,−1).
items.strategy: Compute the inverse pullback on coordinates and use Laurent-monomial independence for the weight decomposition; apply the grading lemma and the embedding theorem to the generating submodule span(x,y).

items.title: An abstract group action need not be an algebraic action
items.statement: The claim that every abstract action of the group of complex points of an affine algebraic group on an affine algebraic set is algebraic and induces a rational coordinate-ring representation is false: G=(C,+) acts on A^1 abstractly by g·x=x+ḡ, each g acts by a polynomial, but the joint map is not a morphism and the coordinate subspace span(1,z) has nonregular matrix coefficient −ḡ.
items.strategy: Show the action is a group action with polynomial individual translations, rule out regularity of the joint map by restriction along g↦(g,0) (a polynomial agreeing with ḡ on R but failing at i), and show no finite-dimensional stable subspace containing z can have regular matrix entries.

items.title: The additive translation action embeds equivariantly as a parabola
items.statement: For G=(C,+) acting on A^1 by g·x=x+g, W=span(1,z,z²) is a generating rational coordinate submodule; evaluation embeds x as (1,x,x²)∈W*≅A³ with closed image a=1, c=b², and the ambient action is linear: g(a,b,c)=(a, b+ga, c+2gb+g²a).
items.strategy: Compute the inverse pullback on 1, z, z² to see W is stable with polynomial matrix entries; apply the embedding theorem and compute the dual linear action and the closed parabola image with inverse x=b.
